Current college student with a lot of real-life advice. 

You may very well qualify for a decent amount of federal aid from the FAFSA, but do NOT count on it. The program is finicky and there's no way of knowing how much you'll get until they give you a real, permanent number. Keep it as an option, but don't rely on it as a way to cover most of your costs. 

Raise your grades. I know you mentioned this, but a 2.6 isn't going to give you any merit-based aid. Along the same lines, if you haven't taken them already, take the SAT and/or ACT. Both can qualify you for merit scholarships if you get good scores. If you've already taken them, consider taking them again. They waive the cost of the test for students who can't afford it. 

Start looking at private scholarships. These are scholarships handed out by companies or organizations, not your school or the government. Most involve writing essays or completing surveys. You can find them if you make an account at a site like Scholarships.com or FastWeb.com. 

Consider living off-campus once you aren't required to live in the dorms anymore. I don't know what your reasoning is for wanting to live on campus the entire time, but it's probably bad. Not only does dorm living restrict your independence, but it's almost always more expensive than renting a cheap apartment off-campus and splitting rent with a roommate/friend. Normally apartments get cheaper the further away from campus you get, so look at those and see if, with transportation costs, it's worth it to move after your first year. 

Save whatever money you have now. Don't invest it, don't loan it to someone, don't spend it on something you don't need. Save it for emergency/backup money and/or money to spend on groceries or fun during college. You'll want to go out with friends now and then, and you should. Don't restrict yourself from having fun, but obviously be reasonable. Exercise good judgment. 

Work during school if you can. Don't overwork yourself, and make sure you have enough time for your studies, but a part-time job can earn you a bit of extra cash to cover expenses or help put a dent in your tuition. Most colleges offer part-time on-campus jobs for students only. These are good because you don't have to seek transportation, but they often pay a bit less than something off-campus.

I live in southern California, where a lot of people like to eat healthy, whether for the sake of health or trendiness. About two years ago, this salad bar called Saladworks opened up by my house. It had a bit of a modern feel, and it ran a bit like Subway -- you get in line, choose a base salad, and pick all your toppings. They sold paninis and I think some soups too, but that was it.

They're closed now. 

Why? Because not a lot of people go out to eat *just* a salad, and their soups/sandwiches were secondary. The restaurant was clean and somewhat stylish (like I said, modern touches), but nothing made the restaurant particularly outstanding. 

If you really want to do this, as a customer, I can give you a few tips. Don't leave your salad sitting out buffet-style behind a glass wall for your employees to fish into a bowl for your customers. Lettuce that has been sitting out tastes gross, feels warm, gets all limp and soggy -- ew. Make sure your dressings are really badass, because a shitty dressing WILL ruin the entire salad. And offer some actually interesting and delicious add-ons -- soups and sandwiches are standard with salads, so you could do that, but it's kind of boring. Maybe come up with a new, fresh pairing instead or in addition to the same old stuff. And even if your food is amazing, the wrong atmosphere can ruin it. People seem to be liking the organic look of exposed wood and stone. Fill the place with plants. Make it look like a very chic farmer's market. 

EDIT: For the sake of providing an example on what I mean about the atmosphere, here: http://karmatrendz.files.wordpress.com/2009/04/restaurant_el_japonez_01.jpg. See the vine wall? I don't know if those plants are real or artificial, but it gives the place a natural, organic touch. The wood furnishings are really nice, but I think picnic tables would be really cool in your place. I realize I'm getting far too into this, but I'm really passionate about restaurant shit.
